verdict.reasoning: The patient reports feeling unwell for four days with symptoms including a sore throat that is resolving, runny nose/congestion, a new dry cough, and fatigue. This is supported by the transcript: 'I've been feeling kind of uh under the weather for the past four days... sore throat and runny nose... starting to cough... kind of uh bad and tired.'
The patient mentions experiencing night sweats, headaches, and muscle pain. The transcript states: 'I'm also having uh night sweats... headaches... general muscle pain or aches, joint pain.'

The patient had a fever early on, now settling with paracetamol and ibuprofen. The transcript states: 'I had some fever in the beginning, but it's now sort of uh going down. I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that.'

The patient reports dyspnea on exertion, no chest pain, and no shortness of breath at rest. The transcript states: 'I feel a bit winded on exertion... no pain in chest... when you're resting, there's no problem.'

The patient reports no ear pain or discharge, no photophobia or vision changes, no nausea or vomiting, normal bowel and urine habits, and no rash. The transcript confirms: 'No, you don't feel blocked, or any discharge coming out of your ears... No, I don't think so... No, none of that... Are your bowels working OK? Uh yeah, yeah... You're passing urine OK? Yeah, yeah... any funny rashes at all, on your skin? Um no, no.'
The patient reports decreased appetite with increased oral fluid intake. The transcript states: 'I've been drinking a lot more than the usual... maybe a bit less than what I would usually have.'

The patient mentions a sick contact with a coworker exhibiting upper respiratory infection symptoms, exposed via colleague with children in kindergarten. The transcript states: 'I think I, it all started with, uh, this colleague of mine, she just kept sneezing next to me... I think her kids are catching something from the uh from their kindergarten.'

The patient reports no past medical or surgical history. The transcript states: 'are you otherwise fit and well? Or do you have any other medical problems I should be aware of? Um, so otherwise that, uh, I'm I'm fine.'
The patient is taking paracetamol and ibuprofen. The transcript states: 'I've been taking some Paracetamol and Ibuprofen for that.'
The patient reports no known drug allergies. The transcript states: 'any allergies at all to any medications, I should be aware of? Um, no.'
The patient's grandmother has Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. The transcript states: 'my grandma has diabetes... I think it's type two.'
The patient's great-grandfather had eczema. The transcript states: 'one of my uh, great grandads had an eczema.'
The patient lives alone and works as an accountant. The transcript states: 'I live alone... I'm an, I'm an accountant.'
The patient is an occasional cigar smoker and drinks alcohol occasionally. The transcript states: 'yeah occasionally, you know, cigars... occasionally yeah I would have some.'

The patient has an acute viral upper respiratory infection with a 4-day course, sore throat leading to congestion and dry cough, fever improving with medications, headache, myalgias, and night sweats; dyspnea only with exertion, no chest pain or shortness of breath at rest. The transcript supports all these details.

The patient is advised to rest and increase fluid intake, and to take off work for 1-2 days. The transcript states: 'I'd probably advise you taking a day or two off work if you can... pushing fluids and make yourself well-hydrated.'
The patient is advised to continue paracetamol and ibuprofen as needed for fever and aches. The transcript states: 'Continue with the regular Paracetamol, Ibuprofen.'
Improvement is expected over approximately 7-10 days. The transcript states: 'these normally last about seven to days and just gets better really, um over time.'
The patient is advised to follow-up next week if not improving. The transcript states: 'if next week you're still not better, I'd like you to come back and see me.'

The patient is advised to return sooner for red flags such as high fever, worsening shortness of breath, or chest pain. The transcript states: 'if you have a high fever, or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner.'
